SK2233 The Type passed cannot satisfy what the API asks for

Enum.GetValues(typeof(Widget)) on a type that is not an enum, Attribute.GetCustomAttribute(m, typeof(Widget)) on a type that is not an attribute, Activator.CreateInstance(typeof(IWidget)) on an interface — each throws on every input.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0
ReSharperPossibleMistakenSystemTypeArgument (resharper_possible_mistaken_system_type_argument_highlighting)

Why

The API states which type it needs in its own documentation and enforces it with a run-time ArgumentException, and typeof(…) states which type it was given right there in the source. Both halves of the contradiction are visible at build time and the compiler relates neither to the other, because Type is Type. ⚠ The failure is total, not conditional: there is no input on which Enum.GetValues(typeof(Widget)) succeeds, so this is not a risk being flagged but a line that cannot work. That is what makes it worth an error-adjacent severity on a rule that never guesses. ⚠ `SK2181` is the neighbouring half and does not overlap. SK2181 reports GetType() called on something that is already a Type — the wrong operation. SK2182 reports a type identified by comparing its name to a string — the wrong test. This one reports the wrong type, in a position where the API says what the right one would have to be.

Example

Instead of:

foreach (var value in Enum.GetValues(typeof(Widget))) { }
var instance = Activator.CreateInstance(typeof(IWidget));

Write:

foreach (var value in Enum.GetValues(typeof(WidgetKind))) { }
var instance = Activator.CreateInstance(typeof(Widget));

When it does not fire

⚠ A closed table of four contracts, matched by parameter *name* and never by index, which is the same discipline taint.json uses and for the same reason: an overload that inserts a parameter shifts every index and changes nothing about a name. System.Enum's enumType must be an enum; the attributeType of Attribute, MemberInfo, ICustomAttributeProvider and CustomAttributeExtensions must derive from System.Attribute; Delegate.CreateDelegate's type must derive from System.Delegate; and Activator.CreateInstance's type must not be an interface, an abstract class or a static class. ⚠ The argument must be a written `typeof(…)`. A Type arriving in a variable is whatever a caller put there and is invisible from here — the same reason SK5001 refuses to treat a parameter as a source. ⚠ An unresolved type, a type parameter and `dynamic` are all declined, because the operand's kind is then not a fact: typeof(T) inside a generic method names a different type at every instantiation, and a T constrained struct, Enum is an enum at every one of them. ⚠ `typeof(Attribute)` itself is not reported, because GetCustomAttribute(member, typeof(Attribute)) means "any attribute" and is exactly right; the test is derives-from-or-equals, not derives-from. ⚠ `SK1035` and this rule cannot both fire. SK1035 offers Enum.GetValues<T>() and requires the argument to be an enum, since the generic overload is constrained struct, Enum; this rule requires it not to be. ⚠ hasFix: false. Which type was meant is the only thing that would repair the line and it is not written anywhere in the file — SK5001 carries the same disposition for the same reason. ⚠ `CA2263` overlaps one row of the table and not the way it was expected to, and the measurement is worth stating because it reverses the obvious guess. Probed on SDK 10.0.400: CA2263 ("prefer the generic overload") fires on Enum.GetValues, Enum.GetNames, Enum.Parse and Activator.CreateInstance when the operand does satisfy the constraint, and goes silent on Enum.GetValues(typeof(NotAnEnum)) and on Attribute.GetCustomAttribute(…, typeof(NotAnAttribute)) — it needs a valid generic overload to suggest, and there is none. So on the enum, attribute and delegate rows the two are disjoint. The one exception is Activator.CreateInstance(typeof(IWidget)), where CA2263 does fire on the same span; it is off by default, its category is usage rather than correctness, and its advice there — Activator.CreateInstance<T>() — does not compile for an interface. The row is kept for that reason: withdrawing it would leave a project at AnalysisMode=All holding only the wrong advice.
